tex_content.html:
\begin{example} \end{example}[A weak derivative that exists] ↗ def:weak-partial-derivative 1. ch5:5.2-ex-1\group Sobolev Spaces

Let $n = 1$, $U = (0,2)$, and \[ u(x) = \begin{cases} x & \text{if } 0 < x \le 1 \\ 1 & \text{if } 1 \le x < 2. \end{cases} \] Define \[ v(x) = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } 0 < x \le 1 \\ 0 & \text{if } 1 < x < 2. \end{cases} \] Let us show $u' = v$ in the weak sense. To see this, choose any $\phi \in C_c^\infty (U)$. We must demonstrate \[ \int _0^2 u\phi ' \, dx = -\int _0^2 v\phi \, dx. \] But we easily calculate \[ \int _0^2 u\phi ' \, dx = \int _0^1 x\phi ' \, dx + \int _1^2 \phi ' \, dx \] \[ = -\int _0^1 \phi \, dx + \phi (1) - \phi (1) = -\int _0^2 v\phi \, dx, \] as required. \end{example}
